t: #3648 Minimum Sensors to Cover Grid — Ceiling Division
o: A sensor covers a (2k+1)×(2k+1) square of cells (Chebyshev ball). Covering the grid with axis-aligned squares of side s = 2k+1 optimally partitions rows into ⌈n/s⌉ bands and columns into ⌈m/s⌉ bands, needing the product. Optimality: each sensor covers at most s rows, so ⌈n/s⌉ sensor-bands are necessary along rows, and similarly for columns; placing sensors at the band corners achieves it. For k = 0 the formula gives n·m, correct since each sensor covers one cell.
k: Chebyshev radius k ⇒ coverage is a square of side 2k+1.
Lower bound: ⌈n/(2k+1)⌉ vertical strips × ⌈m/(2k+1)⌉ horizontal strips.
Tiling strips achieves the bound, so the answer is the product of ceilings.

a.i: Answer = ⌈n/(2k+1)⌉ · ⌈m/(2k+1)⌉, computed with integer ceiling division. Both the lower-bound argument and the explicit strip placement confirm optimality.

w: State the necessity argument (each sensor spans ≤ 2k+1 rows/columns) and the construction (centers on a (2k+1)-spaced lattice anchored at a corner) — together they prove optimality. Pitfall: using Euclidean-distance intuition (circles/diamonds) instead of Chebyshev squares. Follow-up: minimum sensors if sensors may stick out past the grid (same formula), or if some cells are blocked.
